title: TC003-verify_post_orders_endpoint_creates_orders_with_idempotency
description: Test the POST /orders endpoint to confirm it creates orders correctly for one or multiple stores, respects the Idempotency-Key header to prevent duplicate orders, and requires user authentication.
code:
import requests
import uuid
import sys

BASE_URL = "http://localhost:8000"
TIMEOUT = 30.0

def test_verify_post_orders_endpoint_creates_orders_with_idempotency():
    session = requests.Session()
    created_order_ids = []

    def login(email, password):
        url = f"{BASE_URL}/identity/login"
        resp = session.post(url, json={"email": email, "password": password}, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert resp.status_code == 200, f"Login failed: {resp.status_code} {resp.text}"
        data = resp.json()
        assert "access_token" in data, f"No access_token in login response: {data}"
        return data["access_token"]

    token = login("ana@utb.edu.co", "Comprador-2026")
    auth_headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

    try:
        # 1) Unauthorized request is rejected (no Authorization)
        idemp_key = str(uuid.uuid4())
        url = f"{BASE_URL}/orders"
        headers_no_auth = {"Idempotency-Key": idemp_key, "Content-Type": "application/json"}
        resp = session.post(url, json={"items":[{"product_id":4,"cantidad":1}]}, headers=headers_no_auth, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert resp.status_code == 401, f"Expected 401 for unauthenticated POST /orders, got {resp.status_code}: {resp.text}"
        www_auth = resp.headers.get("WWW-Authenticate", "")
        assert www_auth.lower().startswith("bearer"), f"Expected WWW-Authenticate: Bearer header for 401, got: {www_auth}"

        # 2) Request without Idempotency-Key is rejected (422 or 400)
        resp = session.post(url, json={"items":[{"product_id":4,"cantidad":1}]}, headers=auth_headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert resp.status_code in (400, 422), f"Expected 400 or 422 when missing Idempotency-Key, got {resp.status_code}: {resp.text}"

        # 3) Create a single-store order with a fresh Idempotency-Key
        idemp_single = str(uuid.uuid4())
        headers_single = {**auth_headers, "Idempotency-Key": idemp_single}
        body_single = {"items":[{"product_id":4,"cantidad":1}]}
        resp = session.post(url, json=body_single, headers=headers_single, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert resp.status_code in (200,201), f"Unexpected status creating order: {resp.status_code} {resp.text}"
        orders = resp.json()
        assert isinstance(orders, list) and len(orders) == 1, f"Expected list of 1 order, got: {orders}"
        first_order = orders[0]
        assert "id" in first_order, f"Created order missing id: {first_order}"
        assert "items" in first_order and any(item.get("product_id")==4 for item in first_order["items"]), f"Order items do not include product 4: {first_order.get('items')}"
        created_order_ids.extend([first_order["id"]])

        # 4) Repeat the same POST with the same Idempotency-Key -> should return same order(s) (no duplicate)
        resp = session.post(url, json=body_single, headers=headers_single, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert resp.status_code in (200,201), f"Unexpected status on idempotent POST: {resp.status_code} {resp.text}"
        orders_repeat = resp.json()
        assert isinstance(orders_repeat, list) and len(orders_repeat) == 1, f"Expected same single order, got: {orders_repeat}"
        assert orders_repeat[0].get("id") == first_order.get("id"), f"Idempotent POST returned different order id: {orders_repeat[0].get('id')} vs {first_order.get('id')}"

        # 5) Create a multi-store order (products from two different stores)
        idemp_multi = str(uuid.uuid4())
        headers_multi = {**auth_headers, "Idempotency-Key": idemp_multi}
        # product 4 -> tienda 1, product 27 -> tienda 2 (per PRD/test plan)
        body_multi = {"items":[{"product_id":4,"cantidad":1},{"product_id":27,"cantidad":2}]}
        resp = session.post(url, json=body_multi, headers=headers_multi, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert resp.status_code in (200,201), f"Unexpected status creating multi-store order: {resp.status_code} {resp.text}"
        orders_multi = resp.json()
        assert isinstance(orders_multi, list) and len(orders_multi) >= 2, f"Expected at least 2 orders for multi-store request, got: {orders_multi}"

        # Validate each store's order contains expected items
        # We map product_id to presence in returned orders
        found_products = set()
        multi_ids = []
        for o in orders_multi:
            assert "id" in o, f"Order missing id in multi-store response: {o}"
            multi_ids.append(o["id"])
            items = o.get("items", [])
            for it in items:
                pid = it.get("product_id")
                if pid in (4,27):
                    found_products.add(pid)
        assert 4 in found_products and 27 in found_products, f"Multi-store response missing products 4 or 27: found {found_products}"
        created_order_ids.extend(multi_ids)

    finally:
        # Cleanup: attempt to cancel all created orders
        for oid in set(created_order_ids):
            try:
                cancel_url = f"{BASE_URL}/orders/{oid}/cancel"
                resp = session.post(cancel_url, headers=auth_headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)
                # Accept 200 as success; 400/404/403 might mean already cancelled or not allowed, but log them
                if resp.status_code not in (200, 400, 404, 403):
                    print(f"Warning: cancel order {oid} returned unexpected status {resp.status_code}: {resp.text}", file=sys.stderr)
            except requests.RequestException as e:
                print(f"Error cancelling order {oid}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_verify_post_orders_endpoint_creates_orders_with_idempotency()
    print("TC003 completed")

import requests
import sys

BASE_URL = "http://localhost:8000"
TIMEOUT = 30


def test_post_identity_login_endpoint_authenticates_users():
    session = requests.Session()

    # Successful login cases to verify tokens and /identity/me
    valid_accounts = [
        ("ana@utb.edu.co", "Comprador-2026"),                 # buyer
        ("admin.antojos@utb.edu.co", "Tienda-2026"),          # store admin
        ("admin@utb.edu.co", "Admin-Demo-2026"),              # general admin (supervisor)
    ]

    for email, password in valid_accounts:
        try:
            resp = session.post(
                f"{BASE_URL}/identity/login",
                json={"email": email, "password": password},
                timeout=TIMEOUT,
            )
        except requests.RequestException as e:
            assert False, f"Request failed for {email}: {e}"

        assert resp.status_code == 200, (
            f"Expected 200 for valid credentials ({email}), got {resp.status_code}: {resp.text}"
        )

        try:
            data = resp.json()
        except ValueError:
            assert False, f"Login response for {email} is not valid JSON: {resp.text}"

        assert "access_token" in data, f"access_token missing in login response for {email}: {data}"
        assert "expires_in" in data, f"expires_in missing in login response for {email}: {data}"

        token = data["access_token"]
        headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}

        # Verify token works with /identity/me
        try:
            me_resp = session.get(f"{BASE_URL}/identity/me", headers=headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        except requests.RequestException as e:
            assert False, f"Request to /identity/me failed for {email}: {e}"

        assert me_resp.status_code == 200, (
            f"Expected 200 from /identity/me for {email}, got {me_resp.status_code}: {me_resp.text}"
        )

        try:
            me_data = me_resp.json()
        except ValueError:
            assert False, f"/identity/me response for {email} is not valid JSON: {me_resp.text}"

        # Ensure the returned identity corresponds to the logged-in email when provided
        if "email" in me_data:
            assert me_data["email"] == email, (
                f"/identity/me returned email {me_data['email']} but expected {email}"
            )

    # Invalid credential case: wrong password
    wrong_password_email = "ana@utb.edu.co"
    wrong_password = "wrong-password-123"
    try:
        invalid_resp = session.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/identity/login",
            json={"email": wrong_password_email, "password": wrong_password},
            timeout=TIMEOUT,
        )
    except requests.RequestException as e:
        assert False, f"Request failed for invalid credentials test: {e}"

    # Login with invalid credentials should not succeed
    assert invalid_resp.status_code != 200, (
        f"Invalid credentials unexpectedly succeeded with status 200: {invalid_resp.text}"
    )

    # Expect a client error (commonly 400 or 401 or 422). Accept any 4xx.
    assert 400 <= invalid_resp.status_code < 500, (
        f"Expected 4xx for invalid credentials, got {invalid_resp.status_code}: {invalid_resp.text}"
    )

    # Verify the error response contains an explanatory message
    try:
        err_data = invalid_resp.json()
        # Expect some common keys in error responses
        assert any(k in err_data for k in ("detail", "message", "error", "errors")), (
            f"Invalid-login response JSON missing expected error keys: {err_data}"
        )
        # If there's a textual detail, ensure it mentions credentials or auth
        text_values = " ".join(str(v) for v in err_data.values()).lower()
        assert (
            "invalid" in text_values
            or "cred" in text_values
            or "contrase" in text_values
            or "aut" in text_values
            or len(text_values.strip()) > 0
        ), f"Error JSON does not contain an explanatory message: {err_data}"
    except ValueError:
        # Not JSON; inspect raw text
        body = invalid_resp.text.lower()
        assert (
            "invalid" in body
            or "cred" in body
            or "contrase" in body
            or "aut" in body
        ), f"Invalid-login response body not informative: {invalid_resp.text}"


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        test_post_identity_login_endpoint_authenticates_users()
    except AssertionError as e:
        print("TEST FAILED:", e)
        sys.exit(1)
    print("TEST PASSED")
    sys.exit(0)

import requests
import uuid
import sys

BASE_URL = "http://localhost:8000"
TIMEOUT = 30

def test_get_orders_returns_user_order_history():
    session = requests.Session()
    created_order_ids = []

    try:
        # 1) Login as buyer ana
        login_payload = {"email": "ana@utb.edu.co", "password": "Comprador-2026"}
        r = session.post(f"{BASE_URL}/identity/login", json=login_payload, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert r.status_code == 200, f"Login failed: {r.status_code} - {r.text}"
        token = r.json().get("access_token")
        assert token, f"No access_token in login response: {r.text}"
        headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

        # 2) Create a new order for this user (use product_id 29 as demo product)
        idempotency_key = str(uuid.uuid4())
        order_payload = {
            "items": [{"product_id": 29, "cantidad": 1}],
            "hora_recogida": "12:30"
        }
        headers_post = headers.copy()
        headers_post["Idempotency-Key"] = idempotency_key

        r = session.post(f"{BASE_URL}/orders", json=order_payload, headers=headers_post, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert r.status_code in (200, 201), f"Order creation failed: {r.status_code} - {r.text}"
        created_orders = r.json()
        assert isinstance(created_orders, list), f"Expected list from POST /orders, got: {type(created_orders)}"

        # collect created order ids for cleanup
        for o in created_orders:
            oid = o.get("id") or o.get("order_id") or o.get("pedido_id")
            assert oid, f"Created order missing id field: {o}"
            created_order_ids.append(oid)

        assert created_order_ids, "No order ids returned by POST /orders"

        # 3) GET /orders to retrieve user's order history
        r = session.get(f"{BASE_URL}/orders", headers=headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert r.status_code == 200, f"GET /orders failed: {r.status_code} - {r.text}"
        orders = r.json()
        assert isinstance(orders, list), f"Expected list from GET /orders, got: {type(orders)}"

        # 4) Verify that at least one of the created orders appears in the history with correct details
        matched = None
        for order in orders:
            oid = order.get("id") or order.get("order_id") or order.get("pedido_id")
            if oid in created_order_ids:
                matched = order
                break

        assert matched is not None, f"Created order(s) {created_order_ids} not found in GET /orders response"

        # Validate status (estado), items, pickup time, and total
        estado = matched.get("estado") or matched.get("status")
        assert estado is not None, f"Order missing status/estado: {matched}"
        allowed_states = {"pendiente_pago", "pagado", "en_preparacion", "listo", "entregado", "cancelado"}
        assert estado in allowed_states, f"Unexpected order estado: {estado}"

        items = matched.get("items") or matched.get("detalles") or []
        assert isinstance(items, list), f"Order items is not a list: {items}"
        # find our product in items
        found_item = None
        for it in items:
            pid = it.get("product_id") or it.get("producto_id") or it.get("id_producto")
            cantidad = it.get("cantidad") or it.get("qty") or it.get("cantidad_producto")
            if pid == 29 and int(cantidad) == 1:
                found_item = it
                break
        assert found_item is not None, f"Expected product_id 29 with cantidad 1 not found in order items: {items}"

        # hora_recogida
        hora = matched.get("hora_recogida") or matched.get("pickup_time") or matched.get("hora")
        assert hora is not None, f"Order missing hora_recogida/pickup_time: {matched}"
        # Allow small formatting variations but expect "12:30" present
        assert "12:30" in str(hora), f"Expected hora_recogida to include '12:30', got: {hora}"

        # total: look for common keys and validate it's a positive integer
        total_keys = ["total", "total_centavos", "total_cents", "precio_centavos"]
        total_value = None
        for k in total_keys:
            if k in matched:
                total_value = matched[k]
                break
        # Sometimes total may be nested under resumen or similar
        if total_value is None:
            # try common nested places
            resumen = matched.get("resumen") or matched.get("summary") or {}
            if isinstance(resumen, dict):
                for k in total_keys:
                    if k in resumen:
                        total_value = resumen[k]
                        break

        assert total_value is not None, f"Order total not found in order: checked keys {total_keys} and resumen"
        # ensure it's an integer and > 0
        try:
            total_int = int(total_value)
        except Exception:
            raise AssertionError(f"Order total is not an integer: {total_value}")
        assert total_int > 0, f"Order total should be > 0, got: {total_int}"

        print("TEST PASSED: GET /orders returned the created order with expected status, items, pickup time, and total.")

    except AssertionError:
        # re-raise assertion errors for visibility
        raise
    except Exception as e:
        raise AssertionError(f"Unexpected error during test execution: {e}")
    finally:
        # cleanup: cancel created orders to restore state
        for oid in created_order_ids:
            try:
                cancel_resp = session.post(f"{BASE_URL}/orders/{oid}/cancel", headers=headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)
                # Accept 200 or 204 as success; if already cancelled, allow 400/409 but log
                if cancel_resp.status_code in (200, 204):
                    continue
                else:
                    # Not raising to ensure best-effort cleanup, but surface unexpected responses
                    print(f"Cleanup: cancel order {oid} returned {cancel_resp.status_code}: {cancel_resp.text}", file=sys.stderr)
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"Cleanup: exception cancelling order {oid}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_get_orders_returns_user_order_history()

import requests
import uuid
import sys
import traceback

BASE_URL = "http://localhost:8000"
TIMEOUT = 30.0

def test_verify_post_orders_orderid_cancel_endpoint_cancels_pending_orders():
    """
    TC007:
    - Login as buyer ana@utb.edu.co / Comprador-2026
    - Read inventory for a chosen product (product_id 15)
    - Create an order (Idempotency-Key)
    - Assert order is pendiente_pago and inventory decreased
    - Cancel the order
    - Assert inventory restored
    """
    email = "ana@utb.edu.co"
    password = "Comprador-2026"
    product_id = 15
    order_quantity = 1

    token = None
    order_id = None
    created_order_estado = None

    try:
        # 1) Login
        r = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/identity/login",
                          json={"email": email, "password": password},
                          timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert r.status_code == 200, f"Login failed: {r.status_code} {r.text}"
        data = r.json()
        token = data.get("access_token")
        assert token, f"No access_token in login response: {data}"

        headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}

        # 2) Read initial inventory for product_id
        r = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/inventory/{product_id}", headers=headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert r.status_code == 200, f"GET inventory failed: {r.status_code} {r.text}"
        inv = r.json()
        # Inventory representation may vary; try common keys
        if isinstance(inv, dict):
            initial_qty = inv.get("cantidad")
            if initial_qty is None:
                # Fallback to other possible key
                initial_qty = inv.get("existencias") or inv.get("stock") or inv.get("cantidad_disponible")
        else:
            raise AssertionError(f"Unexpected inventory response shape: {inv}")
        assert isinstance(initial_qty, int), f"Initial quantity not found or not int: {inv}"

        # 3) Create order (POST /orders) with Idempotency-Key
        idempotency_key = str(uuid.uuid4())
        order_payload = {
            "items": [
                {"product_id": product_id, "cantidad": order_quantity}
            ],
            "hora_recogida": "12:00"
        }
        post_headers = headers.copy()
        post_headers["Idempotency-Key"] = idempotency_key

        r = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/orders", json=order_payload, headers=post_headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert r.status_code in (200, 201), f"Create order failed: {r.status_code} {r.text}"
        orders = r.json()
        assert isinstance(orders, list) and len(orders) >= 1, f"Orders response expected list with at least one order: {orders}"

        # Find the order that contains our product_id (each order per store)
        found_order = None
        for o in orders:
            items = o.get("items") or []
            for it in items:
                if it.get("product_id") == product_id:
                    found_order = o
                    break
            if found_order:
                break
        if not found_order:
            # Fallback: take first order
            found_order = orders[0]

        order_id = found_order.get("id") or found_order.get("order_id")
        assert order_id, f"Order id not found in response: {found_order}"

        created_order_estado = found_order.get("estado")
        # Accept either None or actual state, but expect pendiente_pago for new orders
        assert created_order_estado in (None, "pendiente_pago", "por pagar", "por_pagar", "PENDIENTE_PAGO", "pendiente_pago".upper()) or created_order_estado == "pendiente_pago", \
            f"Unexpected initial order estado: {created_order_estado}"

        # 4) Verify inventory decreased by order_quantity
        r = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/inventory/{product_id}", headers=headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert r.status_code == 200, f"GET inventory after order failed: {r.status_code} {r.text}"
        inv_after_order = r.json()
        if isinstance(inv_after_order, dict):
            qty_after = inv_after_order.get("cantidad")
            if qty_after is None:
                qty_after = inv_after_order.get("existencias") or inv_after_order.get("stock") or inv_after_order.get("cantidad_disponible")
        else:
            raise AssertionError(f"Unexpected inventory response shape after order: {inv_after_order}")
        assert isinstance(qty_after, int), f"Quantity after order not found: {inv_after_order}"
        assert qty_after == initial_qty - order_quantity, f"Inventory did not decrease correctly: initial={initial_qty}, after={qty_after}"

        # 5) Cancel the order
        r = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/orders/{order_id}/cancel", headers=headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert r.status_code in (200, 204), f"Cancel order failed: {r.status_code} {r.text}"
        # If 200, check response body for estado; if 204 no body
        canceled_state = None
        if r.status_code == 200:
            resp = r.json()
            canceled_state = resp.get("estado") if isinstance(resp, dict) else None

        # 6) Confirm order is cancelado via GET /orders/{id} if possible
        r_get = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/orders/{order_id}", headers=headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        if r_get.status_code == 200:
            order_after = r_get.json()
            estado_after = order_after.get("estado") or order_after.get("status")
            assert estado_after in ("cancelado", "CANCELADO", "Cancelado"), f"Order estado after cancel is not 'cancelado': {estado_after}"
        else:
            # If GET not available or not 200, rely on cancel response having accepted the operation
            if canceled_state:
                assert canceled_state in ("cancelado", "CANCELADO", "Cancelado"), f"Cancel response did not set estado to cancelado: {canceled_state}"
            else:
                # Accept 204 as success
                assert r.status_code == 204, f"Unexpected response when verifying cancel: {r.status_code} {r.text}"

        # 7) Verify inventory restored to initial_qty
        r = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/inventory/{product_id}", headers=headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert r.status_code == 200, f"GET inventory after cancel failed: {r.status_code} {r.text}"
        inv_after_cancel = r.json()
        if isinstance(inv_after_cancel, dict):
            qty_final = inv_after_cancel.get("cantidad")
            if qty_final is None:
                qty_final = inv_after_cancel.get("existencias") or inv_after_cancel.get("stock") or inv_after_cancel.get("cantidad_disponible")
        else:
            raise AssertionError(f"Unexpected inventory response shape after cancel: {inv_after_cancel}")
        assert isinstance(qty_final, int), f"Final quantity not found: {inv_after_cancel}"
        assert qty_final == initial_qty, f"Inventory was not restored after cancel: initial={initial_qty}, final={qty_final}"

        print("TC007 passed.")
    except Exception as e:
        print("TC007 failed:", str(e))
        traceback.print_exc()
        raise
    finally:
        # Cleanup: ensure order is cancelled if it still exists (best effort)
        if token and order_id:
            try:
                headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}
                # Check current status
                r_check = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/orders/{order_id}", headers=headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)
                if r_check.status_code == 200:
                    st = r_check.json().get("estado") or r_check.json().get("status")
                    if st not in ("cancelado", "CANCELADO", "Cancelado"):
                        # Try cancel again
                        requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/orders/{order_id}/cancel", headers=headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)
                # else: cannot access or already removed
            except Exception:
                # best-effort cleanup, ignore errors
                pass

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_verify_post_orders_orderid_cancel_endpoint_cancels_pending_orders()

    url = f"{BASE_URL}/orders/{order_id}/estado"
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {admin_token}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
    resp = requests.post(url, json={"estado": estado}, headers=headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)
    return resp

def cancel_order(order_id, token):
    url = f"{BASE_URL}/orders/{order_id}/cancel"
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
    resp = requests.post(url, headers=headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)
    return resp

def test_buyer_cannot_cancel_after_payment():
    buyer_token = login(BUYER_EMAIL, BUYER_PASSWORD)
    admin_token = login(ADMIN_EMAIL, ADMIN_PASSWORD)

    order_id = None
    try:
        # Read inventory before placing order
        qty_before = get_inventory_qty(PRODUCT_ID, token=admin_token)

        # Create order as buyer
        orders_resp = create_order(buyer_token, PRODUCT_ID, ORDER_QUANTITY)
        order = find_order_for_product(orders_resp, PRODUCT_ID)
        order_id = order.get("id") or order.get("order_id")
        assert order_id, f"Order id not found in response: {order}"

        # Small delay to allow backend to adjust stock
        time.sleep(0.5)

        qty_after_order = get_inventory_qty(PRODUCT_ID, token=admin_token)

        # Ensure stock decreased by at least the ordered quantity
        decreased = qty_before - qty_after_order
        assert decreased >= ORDER_QUANTITY, (
            f"Inventory did not decrease by expected amount after order. "
            f"before={qty_before}, after={qty_after_order}, expected_decrease>={ORDER_QUANTITY}"
        )

        # Admin advances order to 'pagado'
        resp_estado = advance_order_status(order_id, "pagado", admin_token)
        assert resp_estado.status_code == 200, f"Admin failed to set estado 'pagado': {resp_estado.status_code} {resp_estado.text}"

        # Buyer attempts to cancel -> should get 400
        resp_buyer_cancel = cancel_order(order_id, buyer_token)
        assert resp_buyer_cancel.status_code == 400, (
            f"Buyer cancelling a paid order should return 400, got {resp_buyer_cancel.status_code}: {resp_buyer_cancel.text}"
        )

        # Admin cancels -> should succeed (200)
        resp_admin_cancel = cancel_order(order_id, admin_token)
        assert resp_admin_cancel.status_code == 200, f"Admin cancel failed: {resp_admin_cancel.status_code} {resp_admin_cancel.text}"

        # Small delay to allow backend to restore stock
        time.sleep(0.5)

        qty_after_cancel = get_inventory_qty(PRODUCT_ID, token=admin_token)

        # Ensure stock increased by at least the ordered quantity compared to after order
        restored = qty_after_cancel - qty_after_order
        assert restored >= ORDER_QUANTITY, (
            f"Inventory was not restored after admin cancel. after_order={qty_after_order}, after_cancel={qty_after_cancel}, restored={restored}"
        )

        print("TC023 passed: buyer cannot cancel after payment, admin can cancel and stock restored.")
    finally:
        # Cleanup: ensure order is cancelled by admin if still exists and not canceled
        if order_id:
            try:
                # attempt to cancel as admin; ignore result
                cancel_order(order_id, admin_token)
            except Exception:
                pass

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_buyer_cannot_cancel_after_payment()

import requests

def test_multi_store_order_splits_by_store():
    session = requests.Session()

        data = resp.json()
        assert "access_token" in data, f"No access_token in login response: {data}"
        token = data["access_token"]

        headers = {
            "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}",
            "Idempotency-Key": str(uuid.uuid4()),
            "Content-Type": "application/json"
        }

        # 2) Create an order with product 4 (Antojos -> tienda_id 1) and product 27 (Punto Fit -> tienda_id 2)
        orders_url = f"{BASE_URL}/orders"
        order_payload = {
            "items": [
                {"product_id": 4, "cantidad": 1},
                {"product_id": 27, "cantidad": 1}
            ]
        }

        resp = session.post(orders_url, json=order_payload, headers=headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)
        assert resp.status_code == 201, f"Expected 201 Created, got {resp.status_code}: {resp.text}"
        orders_list = resp.json()
        assert isinstance(orders_list, list), f"Response should be a list of orders: {orders_list}"
        # Expect two orders: one per store
        assert len(orders_list) == 2, f"Expected 2 orders (one per store), got {len(orders_list)}: {orders_list}"

        found_store1 = False
        found_store2 = False

        for order in orders_list:
            # Basic structure checks
            assert "id" in order, f"Order missing id: {order}"
            assert "tienda_id" in order, f"Order missing tienda_id: {order}"
            assert "items" in order and isinstance(order["items"], list) and len(order["items"]) >= 1, f"Order items invalid: {order}"
            assert ("total_centavos" in order and isinstance(order["total_centavos"], int)), f"Order missing total_centavos or not int: {order}"

            order_id = order["id"]
            order_ids.append(order_id)

            tienda_id = order["tienda_id"]
            product_ids_in_order = [item.get("product_id") for item in order["items"]]

            # Validate mapping: product 4 -> tienda 1, product 27 -> tienda 2
            if 4 in product_ids_in_order:
                assert tienda_id == 1, f"Product 4 should be in tienda_id 1 but order {order_id} has tienda_id {tienda_id}"
                found_store1 = True
                # Ensure only product 4 is in this order (or at least that no product from other stores is mixed)
                assert 27 not in product_ids_in_order, f"Order {order_id} mixes products from different stores: {product_ids_in_order}"
            if 27 in product_ids_in_order:
                assert tienda_id == 2, f"Product 27 should be in tienda_id 2 but order {order_id} has tienda_id {tienda_id}"
                found_store2 = True
                assert 4 not in product_ids_in_order, f"Order {order_id} mixes products from different stores: {product_ids_in_order}"

        assert found_store1 and found_store2, f"Did not find expected store orders. found_store1={found_store1}, found_store2={found_store2}"

        print("Test TC027 passed: multi-store order created and split by store as expected.")
    except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
        raise AssertionError(f"HTTP request failed: {e}") from e
    finally:
        # Cleanup: cancel created orders to avoid leaving test data (buyer can cancel pending orders)
        if order_ids:
            cancel_headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
            for oid in order_ids:
                try:
                    cancel_url = f"{BASE_URL}/orders/{oid}/cancel"
                    resp = session.post(cancel_url, headers=cancel_headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)
                    # Accept 200 or 400/404 depending on state; log unexpected failures as assertion but do not raise in finally
                    if resp.status_code == 200:
                        print(f"Cancelled order {oid}")
                    else:
                        print(f"Could not cancel order {oid}: status {resp.status_code} response: {resp.text}")
                except Exception as e:
                    print(f"Error while cancelling order {oid}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)

import requests
import sys

BASE = "http://localhost:8000"
PRODUCT_ID = 14
EMAIL = "admin.antojos@utb.edu.co"
PASSWORD = "Tienda-2026"
TIMEOUT = 30.0

def login(email, password):
    url = f"{BASE}/identity/login"
    resp = requests.post(url, json={"email": email, "password": password}, timeout=TIMEOUT)
    assert resp.status_code == 200, f"Login failed: {resp.status_code} {resp.text}"
    body = resp.json()
    assert "access_token" in body, f"No access_token in login response: {body}"
    return body["access_token"]

def get_inventory_item(product_id, headers):
    url = f"{BASE}/inventory/{product_id}"
    resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)
    assert resp.status_code == 200, f"GET /inventory/{product_id} failed: {resp.status_code} {resp.text}"
    body = resp.json()
    # body may be an object or a list; handle both
    if isinstance(body, dict):
        if "cantidad" in body:
            return body
        # sometimes the product may be nested
        if "data" in body and isinstance(body["data"], dict) and "cantidad" in body["data"]:
            return body["data"]
    if isinstance(body, list):
        for item in body:
            # try common keys
            if item.get("id") == product_id or item.get("product_id") == product_id or item.get("producto_id") == product_id:
                if "cantidad" in item:
                    return item
    raise AssertionError(f"Could not find inventory item {product_id} in response: {body}")

def post_adjust(product_id, payload, headers):
    url = f"{BASE}/inventory/{product_id}/adjust"
    return requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)

def put_inventory(product_id, payload, headers):
    url = f"{BASE}/inventory/{product_id}"
    return requests.put(url, json=payload, headers=headers, timeout=TIMEOUT)

def test_stock_cannot_go_negative():
    token = login(EMAIL, PASSWORD)
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}

    # Read current cantidad
    item = get_inventory_item(PRODUCT_ID, headers)
    assert "cantidad" in item, f"Inventory item missing 'cantidad': {item}"
    initial_cantidad = int(item["cantidad"])

    # Attempt to reduce by more than available: delta = -(cantidad + 1)
    payload_neg_over = {"delta": -(initial_cantidad + 1), "motivo": "merma"}
    resp = post_adjust(PRODUCT_ID, payload_neg_over, headers)
    # Expect 400 for over-decrement
    assert resp.status_code == 400, f"Expected 400 when reducing below zero, got {resp.status_code}: {resp.text}"

    # Verify cantidad unchanged
    item_after = get_inventory_item(PRODUCT_ID, headers)
    assert int(item_after["cantidad"]) == initial_cantidad, (
        f"Cantidad changed after rejected over-decrement: before={initial_cantidad}, after={item_after['cantidad']}"
    )

    # Attempt to set cantidad to -1 with PUT -> expect 422
    resp_put = put_inventory(PRODUCT_ID, {"cantidad": -1}, headers)
    assert resp_put.status_code == 422, f"Expected 422 when setting negative cantidad, got {resp_put.status_code}: {resp_put.text}"

    # delta 0 should be rejected (400 or 422)
    resp_delta_zero = post_adjust(PRODUCT_ID, {"delta": 0, "motivo": "merma"}, headers)
    assert resp_delta_zero.status_code in (400, 422), (
        f"Expected 400 or 422 for delta 0, got {resp_delta_zero.status_code}: {resp_delta_zero.text}"
    )

    # Final verify cantidad unchanged
    final_item = get_inventory_item(PRODUCT_ID, headers)
    assert int(final_item["cantidad"]) == initial_cantidad, (
        f"Cantidad changed after delta=0 or invalid PUT: before={initial_cantidad}, final={final_item['cantidad']}"
    )

    print("TC029 stock_cannot_go_negative: PASSED")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        test_stock_cannot_go_negative()
    except AssertionError as e:
        print("TC029 stock_cannot_go_negative: FAILED")
        print(str(e))
        sys.exit(1)
    except requests.RequestException as e:
        print("TC029 stock_cannot_go_negative: ERROR during HTTP request")
        print(str(e))
        sys.exit(2)

            try:

                    try:
